testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving your commercial vehicle.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: Should be expected on the road.
Could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. Even a cardboard box that seems harmless could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: Know the maximum safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Which gas is dangerous if your exhaust system leaks?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can release carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas, into the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Slow down when surfaces have reduced traction. Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on a wet road.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Check for emergency equipment during a pre-trip inspection. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Complete an after-trip inspection at the end of every trip, day, or tour of duty. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Slow down when surfaces have reduced traction. Reduce your speed by one-half or more when driving on packed snow.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured properly to prevent it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports your vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Problems with this system are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, what must you do?

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a safety belt at all times when driving a commercial truck.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid a hazard?

options.text: You should always steer to the left.
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
You should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder is a good way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support large vehicles.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, they should be used together.
Yes, they should be used together on the front of a vehicle.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: Do not use radial and bias-ply tires together. All tires on a vehicle should be the same type and size.

questions.question: How far can a slack adjuster move from where it attaches to the push rod?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster. Pull them to make sure they do not move more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need to be fixed.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm or attack other drivers or their vehicles
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm or attack other drivers or their vehicles
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm others, physically attack another driver, or damage their vehicle.

questions.question: What problem can a broken exhaust system cause?

options.text: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
It does not cause any problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper. Always inspect your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: If air pressure gets too low, air brakes may stop working. The compressor may not be able to replace air fast enough if you press and release the brake pedal too often.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should a driver do?

options.text: Watch for signs that someone is exiting a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for signs that someone is exiting a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked vehicle or from between parked vehicles without looking. A driver may start their vehicle without realizing you are there.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended, should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Yes, the parking brake should always be used.
Only use it if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
No, using it can damage the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, the parking brake should always be used.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: What must you do to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Give your fingerprints and pass a background check.
Give your employment history from the last five years.
Give a list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
The distance your vehicle travels from when a hazard appears until you see it.
The distance your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Your total stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between when you realize you must brake and when you actually hit the brakes.

questions.question: What are the two markings usually on a front brake limiting valve?
questions.explanation: Some vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible when it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.

questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, at dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to make your vehicle more visible.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tires with tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: During a tire inspection, front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth, and other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you may be an aggressive driver?

options.text: Slowing down and keeping a safe distance from other vehicles.
Making hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Do not be an aggressive driver. Be realistic about travel time, plan for delays, keep a safe distance, and never make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass a slow vehicle on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.
Release the clutch when the engine is almost at idle speed.
Shift into neutral when the engine is almost at idle speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.
questions.explanation: When stopping, apply steady pressure to the brake and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.

questions.question: When you change lanes, what should you do with your turn signal?

options.text: Use it only if another vehicle is close to you.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you signal.

questions.question: In cool weather, what happens as the temperature rises and ice starts to melt?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: As temperature rises and ice melts, the road becomes more slippery. Meltwater sits on top of the ice and reduces traction. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: Why can ice cream trucks be hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks need to stay cold.
Children run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children. Children often do not notice other vehicles when they run to or from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: Do not drive if brake drums have cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: If your license is disqualified, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer.
You must notify your employer within two business days.
You must notify your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must notify your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backward when you start from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: What must be done before transporting an over-length load?

options.text: Alert fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads require special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes as much as possible until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern since it is stopped.
Only a concern if passengers are getting off the bus.
A concern whether or not you can see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A concern whether or not you can see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when driving near a stopped bus. Passengers may be near the bus, and the bus may block your view of them or their view of you.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off the turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on the entire time you are turning. Do not turn it off until you finish the turn.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT need to be in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include trip origin, destination, Vehicle Identification Number, distance traveled, and fuel purchased. It does not need to include information about meals.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and a warm cab can make you drowsy. Exercise and a healthy diet help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the engine oil level, coolant level, and condition of hoses.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: If your brakes are hot after coming down a steep hill, let them cool before using the parking brake. Using the parking brake on hot brakes can damage them.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, you should:
questions.explanation: For a manual transmission vehicle, partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake. This stops the vehicle from rolling backward.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. It shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, a driver should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. Park completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the one in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the one in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. This gives you room to slow down without sudden changes and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: The minimum tire tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, do all of the following except:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check the windshield for cracks or problems that block your view. Check wiper arms for proper spring tension and wiper blades for damage or stiff rubber.

questions.question: One way to avoid being an aggressive driver is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Set realistic expectations for travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set realistic expectations for travel time.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead to allow extra time for traffic. Realistic travel expectations reduce frustration that leads to aggressive driving. Also drive at a safe speed, maintain a good following distance, and avoid making gestures at other drivers.
